numberItems.stem: How many exercises make up the list you may be tested on in the basic control skills test?
numberItems.explanation: You are tested on some (a subset) of 6 exercises: straight line backing, offset back right and left, two parallel parks and the alley dock (p. 12-1).

numberItems.stem: How many things does the examiner score on the basic control skills test?
numberItems.explanation: The examiner scores 4 things: encroachments, pull-ups, looks and final position (p. 12-1).

numberItems.stem: During an exercise your mirror brushes a cone. How is that scored?
options: Not at all, because only the tires count
numberItems.explanation: Touching or crossing a line or cone with any part of the vehicle is an encroachment, and each one counts as 1 error (p. 12-1).

numberItems.stem: On the offset back/left exercise, what is the most looks you may take?
numberItems.explanation: Most exercises allow at most 2 looks; only straight line backing is limited to 1 (p. 12-1).

numberItems.stem: When you climb down from the cab for a look, how must you do it?
options: Facing the vehicle, with 3 points of contact
Facing the vehicle, with 2 points of contact
Facing away from the vehicle, with 3 points of contact
numberItems.explanation: Get out facing the vehicle and keep 3 points of contact the whole time; on a bus, hold the handrail (p. 12-1).

numberItems.stem: At the end of the alley dock, the rear of the vehicle must be within how far of the back of the alley?
numberItems.explanation: Finish with the rear within 3 feet of the back of the alley and the vehicle straight, without touching lines or cones (p. 12-2).

numberItems.stem: How many attempts do you have to pass the vehicle inspection, basic control skills and road tests?
numberItems.explanation: You have 3 attempts in total to pass all three skills tests (p. 11-1).
